body:
WHAT
A top-level brain/ folder is the single source of truth for MAGENTRA's model-facing defaults: system and conditional sections, in-turn reminders, finishing rungs, side-call instructions, tool descriptions and every tool parameter (.describe()) description, and the tool set offered per context. The roughly ten model-facing strings still hard-coded in session.ts (steering prefix, interrupt and error reminders, tool-image notes, "Tool did not run.", hook wrappers, the STANDARDS wrap-up line) become registered prompts with their bytes unchanged. A build step (run by npm run build before tsc -b) compiles brain/ into a generated, gitignored module in engine/protocol, so dist/ and the bundled engine.cjs carry the defaults and no packaged install reads them from disk. User overrides in ~/.magentra/prompts/<id>.txt keep working unchanged on top. Each tool's schema shape (types, required fields) stays in its .ts file; only its prose moves. brain/availability.json names the tool set for "main" and "overdrive"; it ships with every tool except Agent and Workflow, so subagents are switched off by default without deleting their code. Out of scope this phase: the subagent.* prompts and engine/core/src/agent/agents.ts (untouched, listed in brain/README.md as the one exception), and swapping between whole brains.

Layout:
  brain/README.md
  brain/prompts/<group>/<id>.md   frontmatter id, label, channel, where, placeholders; body = text
  brain/tools/<Name>.md           body = description; "## <field>" sections = parameter descriptions
  brain/availability.json         { "main": [...], "overdrive": [...] }

WHY
MAGENTRA's behaviour, for a given model, comes mostly from what the model is told and what it can do. Today that is spread over 8+ source files and partly hard-coded outside the registry. One folder makes it readable, reviewable, and ready to specialize later. Subagents (Agent, Workflow) have zero tests and known defects (BIG-PICTURE §5), so they are withheld rather than deleted: no frame, app/, or pin changes.

WHERE
brain/ (new); a compiler under tools/ or engine/protocol; engine/protocol/src/prompts.ts (registry loads defaults from the compiled brain); every definePrompt site except agents.ts: engine/core/src/agent/prompts.ts, engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts, engine/core/src/runtime/finishing.ts, engine/core/src/runtime/engine.ts, engine/core/src/agent/addons.ts, engine/core/src/agent/tool.ts; engine/tools/src/*.ts (descriptions and .describe() text); ToolRegistry.enabled() and executeToolCalls() for the per-context sets; root package.json build script; .gitignore.

KNOWN CONSEQUENCES
- prompt-registry: its "43 registered prompts" count rises by the number of strings brought into the registry; that record's invariant and test change with this feature.
- a-tool-call-shows-while-it-is-written and context-accounting script an Agent call; with Agent withheld by default their engine harness must opt Agent back in explicitly. Their assertions do not change.
- system-prompt-is-pinned and tool-wire-contract-is-pinned must pass unchanged (the wire pin covers registered tools, not enabled ones).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. The ids in promptCatalog() outside group 6 and the prompt files in brain/prompts are the same set, one to one, and no definePrompt call outside agents.ts carries literal text.
2. Every default in promptCatalog() is byte-identical to its pre-migration text (checked against a catalog dump taken before the move).
3. Every registered tool has exactly one brain/tools file, and every parameter description sent on the wire comes from it.
4. An availability.json entry or a brain/tools file naming an unknown tool fails the build with that name.
5. A tool absent from "main" is not in toolSchemas() and a call to it is refused by name; a tool absent from "overdrive" is withheld only while OVERDRIVE is on. With the shipped brain, Agent and Workflow are withheld in both.
6. system-prompt-is-pinned and tool-wire-contract-is-pinned pass unchanged.
7. The bundled engine.cjs boots and answers session_started with no brain/ folder beside it (artifact-tagged, opt-in).
